the speciation of selenium in mustard seeds is complex due to the occurrence of many Se-containing metabolites and their instability under extraction conditions, which results in a number of artifacts and losses of Se.

the analytical methodology developed in this study allows the identification of a large number of Se-containing metabolites, which are formed by three main mechanisms: the Se-S replacement in the metabolic pathway; oxidation of -SeH bonds; and the chemical reactions of Se-containing molecules with other biomolecules through the functional groups not involving the Se atom.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an efficient methodology for the speciation of Se in plants and the identification of a large variety of Se metabolites in mustard seed.
the development and application of analytical methods for the speciation of selenium in mustard seeds, which is a new and important source of selenium for the food industry.

the development of a novel analytical methodology for speciation of low molecular weight selenium (Se) metabolites based on high resolution high mass accuracy electorspray ionization (MS) tandem mass spectrometric (MS/MS) detection and Se-specific detection using ICP mass spectrometry.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
selenoglucinolates and selenoamides represent the most important class and the most abundant Se species in the black mustard seeds.
the Se chemistry in the black mustard is very complex and involves a large number of Se species with a variety of molecular structures and chemical functions.
the Se speciation in mustard seeds was found to be much more complex than expected.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the analytical methodology developed in the present work was able to characterize a large number of Se species in mustard seeds.
the analytical methodology based on ESI-MS/MS and ICP MS allowed for the identification of 32 Se species, which were grouped into five classes.

the speciation analysis of Se in mustard seeds using high-resolution high mass-accuracy MS and parallel detection with Se-specific detection is a powerful tool for studying the metabolic pathway of Se.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of high-resolution ESI MS/MS allows the comprehensive speciation of Se metabolites in complex matrices, including minor components, and that the use of Se-specific detectors (ICP MS or APCI MS) allows a reliable detection of Se-containing compounds in the complex mixture.

the use of high-resolution high mass-accuracy MS in combination with ICP MS and GC-APCI MS/MS allowed for a detailed characterization of a large number of Se metabolites in plant seeds, including the minor species, which are usually difficult to detect using conventional MS/MS.
the Se speciation in the plant material is highly dependent on the analytical conditions and the methodology used.
